T.topic_fa: لوگویی که «به‌اندازه‌ی کافی خلاقانه نیست» و همه می‌شناسندش: ارزش لوگو از تکرار می‌آید، نه از پیچیدگی
T.topic_en: Not creative enough, impossible to miss: a logo's value is built by years of use, not by how clever it looks
T.central_tension_fa: خیال می‌کنیم لوگوی خوب باید پیچیده و هوشمندانه باشد. ولی دفتر کپی‌رایت آمریکا همین هفته گفت سپر قهوه‌ای و طلایی UPS، یکی از شناخته‌شده‌ترین نشانه‌های دنیا، از شکل‌ها و حروف معمولی ساخته شده و «به‌اندازه‌ی کافی خلاقانه نیست». ارزشش هیچ‌وقت از خلاقیت نیامد؛ از دهه‌ها دیده‌شدن روی هر کامیون و هر جعبه آمد.
T.central_tension_en: We think a good logo has to be clever and intricate. This week the US Copyright Office said UPS's brown-and-gold shield, one of the most recognised marks on earth, is made of ordinary shapes and lettering and isn't 'creative enough' for copyright. Its value never came from cleverness. It came from decades on every truck and every box.
T.working_hook_fa: یکی از معروف‌ترین لوگوهای دنیا، رسماً «خلاقانه نیست».
T.working_hook_en: One of the world's best-known logos just got called 'not creative enough'.

key_sources.claim: Review Board upheld two refusals (shield with 'UPS', and blank shield): no 'creative spark'; common shapes, familiar designs, lettering and minor variations. UPS already holds trademarks for the lettered shield logo and for the dark brown colour used on its vehicles and uniforms.

Review Board (30 Oct) affirmed refusal to register two UPS shield logos: familiar geometric shapes, conventional gradient, ordinary lettering, 'insufficiently creative'; protection depends on 'the resulting expression rather than the effort or decisions involved'; recognition does not establish copyright; trademark rights not addressed; decisions carry no precedential weight.
Board found the brown-and-gold shield logos 'weren't creative enough to warrant copyright protection' (paywalled; summary only).
Confirms the denial for both versions; some well-known logos may not qualify for copyright regardless of commercial value.
Previous shield designed by Paul Rand in 1961; redesigned in 2003 (bow-tied parcel removed). Context only, caption level.
'Nothing original about UPS shield logos': 'uncopyrightable common geometric shapes'; other geometric registrations given no precedential weight.

T.framing_note: News is the spark; the evergreen idea: simple marks earn value through consistent repetition; complexity is not value; effort is not what the customer sees. Be precise: this is a COPYRIGHT registration refusal only. Never say UPS 'lost its logo', 'anyone can copy it' or that the logo is unprotected; trademark rights are untouched (say once: 'it is still their trademark; this was about copyright'). Not legal advice; one board decision. Say 'the US copyright office', not paragraph quotes; on screen no publication names. Don't mock UPS or the designers; the point is a compliment to simplicity. Paul Rand 1961 / 2003 redesign only in caption. Owner takeaway (café, salon, shop, studio): don't pay for a busier logo; pick a simple mark and use it the same way on every cup, bag, sign and post for years; for legal protection ask a trademark lawyer. One number max on screen (e.g. 'since 1961' only if needed). Never name the UAE, Dubai or any emirate. Owner rule from 2026-11-07: use modern, attractive, relevant mockups (motion.md rule 9): blank AI mockup + real logo composited; never AI-draw the UPS logo; label as editorial mockup in caption. Mockups are not UPS ads.

fact_sheet_on_screen_safe: The US Copyright Office review board refused to register two UPS shield logos (blank shield; shield with 'ups') on 30 Oct 2026. [Bloomberg Law, TFL, Law360]
Reason in plain words: common shapes, familiar lettering, standard arrangement: no 'creative spark'. [Bloomberg Law]
Effort and decisions behind it don't count; only the result people see. ['the resulting expression rather than the effort or decisions involved', TFL]
UPS still holds trademarks on the lettered shield and on its dark brown colour (vehicles, uniforms). This was copyright only. [Bloomberg Law]
The shield has been simplified over time: Paul Rand's 1961 shield with a tied parcel; 2003 redesign removed the parcel. [Truck News 2003]
DO NOT say: court, lawsuit, 'UPS lost its logo', 'anyone can copy it', 'owns the colour brown' (say: its brown is trademarked for its vans and uniforms).
